claims.text: USGS recorded a magnitude 7.7 (Mww) earthquake on 9 October 2026 at 17:56:06 UTC, located 12 km WSW of Pitaloza Arriba, Herrera Province, Panama (7.5868°N, -80.769°W) at a depth of 12.6 km. USGS's PAGER system assessed a Red alert, estimating about 4.6 million people exposed to Strong-to-Very-Strong (MMI V-VIII) shaking, with ground-failure alerts of Red for landslide and Orange for liquefaction.

GDACS's event report lists a further Copernicus Emergency Management Service rapid-mapping update for EMSR934 (Los Santos, Panama) dated 16 October 2026 20:15 UTC, indicating the activation remains active a week after the earthquake.

GDACS's earthquake report for this event (event id 1570339, episode 1738684), checked 18 October 2026, now lists Exposed Population at '130 thousand (in MMI>=VII)' and a GDACS Score of 1.4 -- up from the roughly 50,000 recorded a day earlier -- while continuing to rate the event Overall Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact; the maximum observed tsunami wave height remains about 1.09 meters.

PAHO/WHO news article (dated 10 October 2026, with an 11 October dateline in the text): per preliminary information from Panama's Ministry of Health (MINSA), 29 health facilities were affected across eight provinces and the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca following the earthquake; most remain operational, though some have structural or non-structural damage, preventive evacuations, care relocated to tents or temporary modules, or interrupted water/electricity service. No deaths or injuries are reported in the article beyond PAHO's earlier situation-report toll. MINSA's Emergency Operations Coordination Center (CODES) remains active, and PAHO/WHO's Panama office has activated its own emergency response mechanisms to support damage assessment and needs identification.

PAHO's 'Reporte de Situacion #3: Terremotos en Panama' (data as of 18 October 2026): the national government confirmed the first death, 'el fallecimiento de una persona que habia resultado herida durante el evento' (the death of a person who had been injured during the event). Panama's SINAPROC reports 26,018 people directly affected and 7,933 homes evaluated (74% in Los Santos and Herrera) across 10 provinces and the Ngabe-Bugle comarca; 3,827 people remain sheltered in 55 active shelters (69.8% in Veraguas), and 27 people are reported injured. Panama's Ministry of Health (MINSA) reports 219 health facilities reviewed: 142 operational, 38 partially operational, 22 non-operational and 17 pending status, with 30 sites using temporary or adapted spaces. More than 600 aftershocks have been reported by the University of Panama's Institute of Geosciences.

GDACS's earthquake report (event id 1570339, episode 1738684, GLIDE EQ-2026-000188-PAN) rates the event an Overall Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, estimating about 540,000 people within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking, and recorded a tsunami with a maximum observed wave height of about 1.09 meters.

USGS recorded an intense aftershock sequence following the M7.7 mainshock, including a magnitude 6.6 aftershock 14 km W of Río Grande at 20:25 UTC on 9 October and a magnitude 6.0 aftershock 7 km N of La Tronosa at 04:14 UTC on 10 October, plus dozens of additional magnitude 4.5-5.8 aftershocks clustered around Herrera and Los Santos provinces through 11 October.

GDACS's event report lists a new Copernicus Emergency Management Service rapid-mapping activation, EMSR934, triggered 12 October 2026 at 03:45 UTC for Los Santos, Panama, in response to the earthquake.

PAHO's 'Informe de Situacion 1: Terremoto en Panama, Octubre 2026' (dated 11 October 2026): reports 27 people injured with mild-to-moderate injuries who received medical care, and no deaths or missing persons confirmed as of the report's cutoff. The Government of Panama declared a state of emergency on 10 October 2026 to strengthen response, coordination and resource mobilization. Panama Canal operations and vessel traffic continued normally, Tocumen International Airport resumed operations after safety checks, and Metro Lines 1 and 2 were out of service for technical inspections as of the prior cutoff.

USGS's event feed for the earthquake, with Key Points updated 13 October 2026, now assesses the PAGER shaking-impact alert at Orange (automatic PAGER product), estimating about 3.4 million people exposed to Strong-to-Very-Strong (MMI V-VIII) shaking -- down from the initial Red alert and approximately 4.6 million estimate. Ground-failure exposure is now Orange for liquefaction (about 29,000 people, 1-sigma range about 25,558-31,639) and Yellow for landslide (about 180 people, 1-sigma range about 154-200), down from the initial Red landslide / Orange liquefaction alerts. The page records 1,887 'Did You Feel It?' responses with a maximum reported intensity (CDI) of 7.9.

GDACS's earthquake report (event id 1570339, episode 1738684), checked 17 October 2026, now lists Exposed Population as '50 thousand (in MMI>=VII)' -- down sharply from its initial estimate of about 540,000 -- while continuing to rate the event Overall Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact.

USGS's ground-failure product for the earthquake (last updated 18 October 2026, 05:25 UTC) continues to estimate liquefaction population exposure at approximately 49,000 people (Orange alert) and landslide population exposure at approximately 200 people (Yellow alert), unchanged from 17 October 2026.

USGS's earthquake catalog records a magnitude 6.1 aftershock 17 km W of Rio Grande, Panama, at 23:20:36 UTC on 12 October 2026, continuing the aftershock sequence that began with the 9 October magnitude 7.7 mainshock.

description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on 9 October 2026, centered in Herrera Province on the Azuero Peninsula, about 200 km southwest of Panama City. A tsunami warning covering the Pacific coasts of Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala was issued and later cancelled, and an intense aftershock sequence has continued, with more than 600 aftershocks recorded by 18 October. PAHO's Situation Report 3 (18 October) confirms the first death, of a person who had been injured in the earthquake, alongside 27 people injured and no one missing. Panama's civil protection agency (SINAPROC) reports 26,018 people directly affected and 7,933 homes evaluated across 10 provinces and the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca, with 3,827 people still sheltering in 55 active shelters, concentrated in Veraguas. Panama's Ministry of Health reports 219 health facilities reviewed, of which 142 are operational, 38 partially operational and 22 non-operational; the national State of Emergency remains in force.

impact.summary: PAHO's Situation Report 3 (18 October 2026) confirms the first death in the earthquake response -- a person who had been injured in the 9 October event -- alongside 27 injured and no one missing. Panama's SINAPROC reports 26,018 people directly affected and 7,933 homes evaluated across 10 provinces and the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca (74% of evaluated homes in Los Santos and Herrera), with 3,827 people still sheltering in 55 active shelters, 69.8% of them in Veraguas. Panama's Ministry of Health reports 219 health facilities reviewed: 142 operational, 38 partially operational, 22 non-operational and 17 pending status, with 30 sites relying on temporary or adapted spaces. More than 600 aftershocks have been recorded since the mainshock. GDACS's estimate of people exposed to MMI VII+ shaking stands at about 130,000 (GDACS Score 1.4), continuing to rate the event Overall Orange for medium humanitarian impact; USGS's PAGER ground-failure product holds at about 49,000 people exposed to liquefaction hazard (Orange) and about 200 to landslide hazard (Yellow). Panama's national State of Emergency, declared 10 October, remains in force.

name: M7.7 Earthquake, Azuero Peninsula, Panama

updates.text: PAHO's Situation Report 3 (data as of 18 October) confirmed the earthquake's first death -- a person who had been injured in the event -- and reported 26,018 people directly affected, 7,933 homes evaluated, and 3,827 people still sheltering in 55 active shelters; 219 health facilities have been reviewed, 142 fully operational.

PAHO reported Panama's Ministry of Health found 29 health facilities affected across eight provinces and the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca, most still operating; the injury/death toll (27 injured, no deaths) is unchanged. GDACS's MMI VII+ exposure estimate rose to about 130,000 (score 1.4), after an intervening estimate of about 50,000; USGS's ground-failure estimates held steady.

GDACS revised its MMI VII+ exposed-population estimate sharply down to about 50,000 (from ~540,000); USGS's ground-failure product was revised up to ~49,000 people exposed to liquefaction (Orange) and ~200 to landslide (Yellow). A M6.1 aftershock struck near Rio Grande on 12 October, and Copernicus EMS mapping for Los Santos continued through 16 October.

PAHO's first situation report (11 October) recorded 27 injured and no deaths; Panama declared a state of emergency on 10 October. USGS revised its PAGER alert down from Red to Orange, lowering its shaking-exposure estimate to about 3.4 million people and its ground-failure alerts to Orange liquefaction / Yellow landslide (from Red landslide / Orange liquefaction).

GDACS's event report recorded a new Copernicus EMS rapid-mapping activation (EMSR934) for Los Santos, Panama, three days after the mainshock; no confirmed death or injury toll has yet been published by an authoritative source.

USGS recorded a vigorous aftershock sequence, including a magnitude 6.6 aftershock on 9 October and a magnitude 6.0 aftershock on 10 October near Río Grande/La Tronosa, Herrera Province, plus dozens of magnitude 4.5+ aftershocks; no casualty toll has yet been published.
